input.question: How come that you can have periods of time where you remember all your dreams when you wake up, and periods of time where you remember nothing.
input.ground_truth: If you have a sleep schedule that you stick to, you mind makes sure to wrap up all your dreams before you wake up. However, if you start waking up at unusual times, you may wake up smack dab in the middle of a dream. This makes you more likely to remember it. So the periods of time when you remember your dreams should correspond with you altering your sleeping habits while the periods where you can't remember anything should correspond to more stable sleeping habits.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: How come that you can have periods of time where you remember all your dreams when you wake up, and periods of time where you remember nothing.

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your brain is like a little notebook. Sometimes, when you sleep, your brain writes down your dreams really clearly, and when you wake up, you can remember them, like finding a picture you drew the night before.

But sometimes, your brain doesn’t write the dreams very well, or it erases them before you wake up. That’s why sometimes you don’t remember your dreams at all—it’s like trying to remember a drawing that disappeared!

So, it’s normal for your brain to sometimes remember dreams and sometimes not. It just depends on how well your brain keeps the dream picture for you.
